19.0.s.en: 1. The lioness and her two whelps:

19.0.0.en: 1 "Moreover take thou up a lamentation for the princes of Israel, 2 And say, What is thy mother? A lioness: she lay down among lions, she nourished her whelps among young lions. 3 And she brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men. 4 The nations also heard of him; he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt. 5 Now when she saw that she had waited, and her hope was lost, then she took another of her whelps, and made him a young lion. 6 And he went up and down among the lions, he became a young lion, and learned to catch the prey, and devoured men. 7 And he knew their desolate palaces, and he laid waste their cities; and the land was desolate, and the fulness thereof, by the noise of his roaring. 8 Then the nations set against him on every side from the provinces, and spread their net over him: he was taken in their pit. 9 And they put him in ward in chains, and brought him to the king of Babylon: they brought him into holds, that his voice should no more be heard upon the mountains of Israel.

19.0.1.en: Here he offers a lamentation for the kings of Judah, especially the two kings: Jehoahaz, who met his sorrowful fate by being carried captive to Egypt in 608 B.C. after a reign that lasted 3 months, and King Jehoiachin, who was taken captive to Babylon in 597 B.C. after a reign that likewise lasted about 3 months.

19.1.0.en: A. That he does not say "a lamentation for the princes of Judah" or "the kings of Judah" but for "the princes of Israel"... for what befalls one of the two kingdoms befalls the whole people. God looks upon believing mankind as one people: if one member suffers, the rest of the members suffer with it, "and if one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it" (1 Cor 12:27). These two kings did not wrong themselves alone by their sinful conduct, nor the kingdom of Judah alone, but all Israel, who represented the people of God at that time. Thus when one member in us grows weak, the whole body grows weak with it, and when one of the members repents, all heaven rejoices over him! Our worship is a personal relationship with God, but it is not individual, that is, not isolated from the holy congregation, whether the militant or the triumphant, or even the members who will come in the future. It is one Church interacting together in love and the spirit of unity. B. "And say, What is thy mother? A lioness: she lay down among lions, she nourished her whelps among young lions" [2]. She is a queen who lies down in strength among kings, and she is likened to a lioness and not a lion because she is a queen who bears kings and brings them up: "And she brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men. The nations also heard of him; he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt" [3-4]. This is Jehoahaz, who was brought up in a royal family, became king and learned war, but instead of fighting to protect his people he fought his own children to devour them. He worked for himself and not for the kingdom that had raised him and made him king. He proved to be weak and stripped of moral principles; Pharaoh Necho carried him captive down to Egypt, and he never returned to his land.

19.1.1.en: In any case, he is a young lion who protected neither his people nor even himself, but preyed upon his flock...

19.1.2.en: How hard it is for the shepherd to turn into a wolf, and instead of protecting his sheep to slaughter them that he himself may be filled! He should have offered his life as a sacrifice of love for his people, not slaughtered his people for the sake of his own honor or private interests. In this St. Aphrahat says: [Imitate our sweet Shepherd (Jesus), whose life was not dearer to Him than His sheep. Train the young, love the lambs, and carry them in your bosoms, so that when you stand before the Chief Shepherd you may present the flock complete, and He will give you what He promised you: "that where I am, there ye may be also"].

19.1.3.en: And St. Augustine says: [Let us not love ourselves but love Him, and in tending His sheep let us seek what is His and not what is ours... For he who cannot live by himself surely dies if he loves himself. And in this he is not a lover of himself, for by loving himself he loses his life...

19.1.4.en: May the shepherds of the flock not be lovers of themselves, lest they tend the flock as though it were their own property and not as the flock of Christ, seeking material gain as "lovers of money."

19.1.5.en: Or they domineer over the people as profiteers, or seek glory from the honor offered them as the proud, or fall into heresies as blasphemers, and despise the holy fathers as disobedient to parents.

19.1.6.en: And they repay with evil the good done to those whom they wish to reform, lest they perish, as the unthankful.

19.1.7.en: And they kill their own souls and the souls of others as those who are without mercy, and try to distort the characters of the saints as false witnesses, and give free rein to base desires as the unclean, and are always complaining... as the unmerciful.

19.1.8.en: And they know nothing of the service of love, as those who have no compassion; they trouble mankind with their foolish disputes as the obstinate; they do not understand what they say or what they insist upon, as the blind; and they prefer fleshly delights to joy, as lovers of self more than lovers of God.

19.1.9.en: These and other similar vices, whether they all appear together in one person, or one of them dominates one person and another dominates another, appear in one form or another from the starting point of being lovers of themselves. This is the vice against which those who tend the flock of Christ must be on guard, lest they seek what is their own and not what is Jesus Christ's, and use for the fulfillment of their lusts those for whom Christ shed His blood].

19.1.10.en: Jehoahaz preyed upon his sheep instead of defending them and laying down his life for them, so he himself became the prey of the nations; he fell into their snares and was led captive to Egypt. He who tends himself at the expense of his brethren and at the expense of the salvation of his own soul loses even his bodily pleasure and his earthly honor.

19.1.11.en: The matter was repeated with another king, "Jehoiachin," who was no better than the former, but devoured his people and laid waste their cities by his evil conduct, so the land became desolate because of him, and he was carried captive to Babylon.

19.2.0.en: 10 "Thy mother is like a vine, like thee, planted by the waters: she was fruitful and full of branches by reason of many waters. 11 And she had strong rods for the sceptres of them that bare rule, and her stature was exalted among the thick branches, and she appeared in her height with the multitude of her branches. 12 But she was plucked up in fury, she was cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up her fruit: her strong rods were broken and withered; the fire consumed them. 13 And now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty ground. 14 And fire is gone out of a rod of her branches, which hath devoured her fruit, so that she hath no strong rod to be a sceptre to rule. This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation."

19.3.0.en: After offering a lamentation for these two kings, he begins to offer a lamentation for the people of God, who were like a vine planted by the waters of divine grace, so that she was "fruitful and full of branches by reason of many waters" [11]. The nations could not stand against her, but her stem rose high and her branches multiplied... But when she left her God and turned back to idolatry, she was plucked up from her land and carried to Babylon, so she withered by the winds of discipline and lost her fruit through her multiplied sins... Her branches became fuel and she entered into a state of extreme weakness, with none to support her! This is the lamentation over every man who leaves the way of the Lord and runs after the desires of his heart and the pleasures of his body: he is deprived of enjoying the waters of the Holy Spirit, who gives life and bears fruit, and he is removed from the position of sonship to God to become, by his wicked heart and evil life, a stranger and a captive in the land of the enemy (the devil); his branches are broken to become fuel consumed by the flames, and his soul dries up completely like a barren land!

19.3.2.en: * The kings of Israel turned from shepherds into wolves!

19.3.3.en: They preyed upon the flock and practiced the love of power!

19.3.4.en: They sought what was their own and not what belonged to their people!

19.3.5.en: So they perished, and lost all riches and pleasure and honor!

19.3.6.en: * I complain to You about myself!

19.3.7.en: I forgot my kingship and turned to preying; I did not seek love, what belongs to others, but what is for myself!

19.3.8.en: Restore to me the nature of kingship, O King of kings!

19.3.9.en: Teach me love, and I shall become a queen!

20.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, that certain of the elders of Israel came to enquire of the LORD, and sat before me. 2 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 3 "Son of man, speak unto the elders of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Are ye come to enquire of me? As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will not be enquired of by you. 4 Wilt thou judge them, son of man, wilt thou judge them? cause them to know the abominations of their fathers, In the previous year a group of elders came to ask the prophet in the land of captivity about what would happen to the kingdom of Judah and to the captive people at that time, but he directed the speech toward repentance, for the Lord said: "As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will not be enquired of by you" [3]. If you have come to ask me, first remove from yourselves the nature of rebellion that your fathers lived and you live, and then I shall answer your requests.

20.0.1.en: We often cry out to the Lord in time of distress, and He wishes to deliver and longs to save, but He wants the distress to achieve its goal, which is our repentance from the heart and our returning to Him with all the heart! If God delays in answering, it is not out of neglect of us but a sign of His care, for He waits for the sincerity of our repentance that we may profit from the trial. Our rebellious nature needs the fire of affliction that we may turn back to our God and seek Him sincerely.

20.1.0.en: 5 And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day when I chose Israel, and lifted up mine hand unto the seed of the house of Jacob, and made myself known unto them in the land of Egypt, when I lifted up mine hand unto them, saying, I am the LORD your God; 6 In the day that I lifted up mine hand unto them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands: 7 Then said I unto them, Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt: I am the LORD your God. 8 But they rebelled against me, and would not hearken unto me: they did not every man cast away the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt: then I said, I will pour out my fury upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt. 9 But I wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, among whom they were, in whose sight I made myself known unto them, in bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt.

20.2.0.en: The nature of rebellion is not something new in their life, but it has accompanied them since the beginning of their appearance as a people or nation in the land of Egypt. Jacob and his sons entered Egypt as a family and came out as a people under the leadership of the first leader, Moses the prophet. In Egypt, where this nation and people grew, the idols of Egypt were nurtured within their heart. The Lord uncovered the secret of their bondage in Egypt: it was not the hardness of Pharaoh's heart but the perversion of the people's heart: "Then said I unto them, Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt: I am the LORD your God. But they rebelled against me" [7-8]. At the time when God was spying out for them the land flowing with honey and milk, "the glory of all lands" [6], they refused to cast away the abominations of their eyes and to forsake the idols, and yet He did not pour out His wrath on them in the land of Egypt but brought them out with power for the sake of His holy name [9], that He might be glorified in them among the nations.

20.2.1.en: Thus God cares for man from his creation, and He even devised our salvation and our crossing over from the bondage of sin and our being brought into His bosom, the paradise of truth that overflows for the soul with honey and milk, while man is born with the microbe of disobedience running in his blood. Rebellion is a nature we inherited from the disobedience of our first parents; therefore our reform needs a complete change of our nature.

20.3.0.en: 10 Wherefore I caused them to go forth out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the wilderness. 11 And I gave them my statutes, and shewed them my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them. 12 Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them. 13 "But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they walked not in my statutes, and they despised my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; and my sabbaths they greatly polluted: then I said, I would pour out my fury upon them in the wilderness, to consume them. 14 But I wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen, in whose sight I brought them out. 15 Yet also I lifted up my hand unto them in the wilderness, that I would not bring them into the land which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands; 16 Because they despised my judgments, and walked not in my statutes, but polluted my sabbaths: for their heart went after their idols. 17 Nevertheless mine eye spared them from destroying them, neither did I make an end of them in the wilderness.

20.4.0.en: How many were God's gifts in the wilderness! He gave them fresh food every day for nothing, so that they needed neither to plow the land and clear it, nor to sow and reap, nor to gather the harvest and prepare the food. And He gave them a rock that gushed forth sweet water and followed them wherever they went, a thing that costs man much, especially in the desert! They lacked neither new clothes nor shoes, nor medicines to heal the sick... He cared for them in every great and small thing, and yet in His reproach to them He mentioned nothing of this but concentrated on two things that He considered the best He had given them: the divine commandment and His sabbaths, for He says: "And I gave them my statutes, and shewed them my judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them. Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them" [11-12]. He gave them the commandment as His own statutes and judgments, and the sabbaths as His own sabbaths. By the commandment man lives, and by the sabbaths he is sanctified. This, in God's view, was the summit of what He did for them in the wilderness.

20.4.1.en: As for the commandment, it is a sign of God's love for man and His care, for He did not accept to make him like the irrational creatures, walking as the nature given to him by God dictates, but gave him free will, and granted him the commandment as a sign of this freedom: he may accept life with God and he may refuse it. As Tertullian says: [He enabled him, as a human being, to boast that he alone was worthy to receive commandments from God, as a being capable of reason and knowledge, who restrains himself quietly with the bonds of reasoning freedom, subject to God, to whom He subjected all things].

20.4.2.en: The commandment is also the sphere in which man surrenders his will to the Lord by obedience, so that he receives the divine will working in him. For in accepting the commandment he accepts the word of God, who works in him. Therefore the Lord says: "If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free" (Jn 8:31, 33), "the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life" (Jn 6:63). And St. Mark the Ascetic says: [God is hidden in His commandments, so whoever seeks Him finds Him in them].

20.4.3.en: As for the sabbaths, which God gave us for our sanctification, they point to the Lord Christ Himself, who came on the seventh day as the mystery of our true rest. For the word "sabbath" means in Hebrew "rest," and we have no rest except in Christ Jesus. He is the mystery of the Sabbath: in Him the Father rested in us, since He found Him, as our representative, the object of His pleasure, and in Him we rested in the Father, since we find in Him the Father's bosom receiving us. The Lord Christ is the mystery of our sabbath and the mystery of our sanctification!

20.4.4.en: St. Augustine divides the history of the world's salvation into the days of the week as follows:

20.4.5.en: The first day: from Adam to the Flood; the second day: from the Flood to Abraham; the third day: from Abraham to David; the fourth day: from David to the captivity; the fifth day: from the captivity to the Incarnation of Christ; the sixth day: from the Incarnation to the great day of the Lord; the seventh day: the great day of the Lord, in which mankind finds its rest in Christ Jesus our Lord. By this the Lord brings us into a life without end, in which our souls rest with our bodies. "There we shall rest and see, see and love, love and praise. This is what shall be in the end that has no end, for what other end have we for ourselves than to attain the Kingdom that has no end?"!

20.4.6.en: St. Clement of Alexandria says: [We keep the spiritual Sabbath until the coming of the Savior, since we have rested from sin].

20.5.0.en: The Lord gave them His commandment as a sign of His esteem for man above every other earthly creature, but man despised it and did not walk in it. And He gave him His sabbaths for his sanctification, but man greatly polluted the sabbaths of the Lord [13]. And yet the Lord says: "Nevertheless mine eye spared them from destroying them, neither did I make an end of them in the wilderness" [17]. This is God's longsuffering toward us and His love for us!

20.6.s.en: 4. The rebellion of the new generation in the wilderness:

20.6.0.en: 18 But I said unto their children in the wilderness, Walk ye not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols: 19 I am the LORD your God; walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them; 20 And hallow my sabbaths; and they shall be a sign between me and you, that ye may know that I am the LORD your God. 21 Notwithstanding the children rebelled against me: they walked not in my statutes, neither kept my judgments to do them, which if a man do, he shall even live in them; they polluted my sabbaths: then I said, I would pour out my fury upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the wilderness. 22 Nevertheless I withdrew mine hand, and wrought for my name's sake, that it should not be polluted in the sight of the heathen, in whose sight I brought them forth. 23 I lifted up mine hand unto them also in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries; 24 Because they had not executed my judgments, but had despised my statutes, and had polluted my sabbaths, and their eyes were after their fathers' idols. 25 Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live; 26 And I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that openeth the womb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might know that I am the LORD.

20.6.1.en: God again affirmed to the new generation that was born in the wilderness that they should not walk in the spirit of their fathers, who came out of Egypt carrying its idols in their heart, but should walk in His statutes, keep His judgments and do them, and hallow His sabbaths as the sign of the covenant between Him and them. Yet the children were no less rebellious than their fathers. They were drawn to the idols of their fathers and not to the Lord their God. And in spite of all this, for His name's sake He did not wish to pour out His wrath on them in the wilderness, lest He be despised in the sight of the nations.

20.6.2.en: Perhaps some will object to the divine saying:

20.7.0.en: "Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live; and I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that openeth the womb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might know that I am the LORD" [25-26].

20.7.1.en: When sinners insist on disobedience, He gives them His commandments and judgments for their salvation [11], but He does not compel them to keep them... If they continue in their insistence, He gives them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient (Rom 1:28).

20.7.2.en: The word "gave" here means "permitted them" to accept the statutes and judgments of pagan worship, so that they practiced passing through the fire... and perished.

20.8.0.en: 27 "Therefore, son of man, speak unto the house of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Yet in this your fathers have blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me. 28 For when I had brought them into the land, for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to them, then they saw every high hill, and all the thick trees, and they offered there their sacrifices, and there they presented the provocation of their offering: there also they made their sweet savour, and poured out there their drink offerings. 29 Then I said unto them, What is the high place whereunto ye go? And the name thereof is called Bamah unto this day.

20.8.1.en: He prolonged the period of their wandering in the wilderness to forty years that they might forget the idols of Egypt which they had carried with them in their hearts, and brought them into a new land, and behold, they adopted the pagan worship of this country and set up their worship on the high places like the people of the region. Instead of being the holy people of God, glorifying God in the midst of the nations, they went after the uncleanness of the nations.

20.9.s.en: 6. Their rebellion in the days of Ezekiel:

20.9.0.en: 30 "Wherefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations? 31 For when ye offer your gifts, when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day: and shall I be enquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will not be enquired of by you. 32 And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.

20.9.1.en: The process of rebellion is not a historical process but a present reality: it began with the appearance of the people as a nation, pursued them in the wilderness to the new generation, burned all the more when they entered the Promised Land, and is still working in them even at the time when Ezekiel was speaking with the elders. The Lord rebukes them: "Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations? For when ye offer your gifts, when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day" [30-31]. Therefore the answer was, "As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will not be enquired of by you." He does not accept their question nor answer their requests until their hearts change. He disciplines them with a mighty hand and a stretched out arm, pours out His wrath on them, scatters them and pleads with them openly [33-35].

20.10.s.en: 7. Their rebellion in the land of captivity:

20.10.0.en: 33 As I live, saith the Lord GOD, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you: 34 And I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out. 35 And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. 36 Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you, saith the Lord GOD. 37 And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: 38 And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me: I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 39 "As for you, O house of Israel, thus saith the Lord GOD; Go ye, serve ye every one his idols, and hereafter also, if ye will not hearken unto me: but pollute ye my holy name no more with your gifts, and with your idols.

20.11.0.en: In all this He does not take vengeance but disciplines in order to bring them into a new covenant. "And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me" [37-38]. He brings them into the wilderness, not the wilderness of Sinai as He did with their fathers, but into a state of dryness and drought within the captivity and their scattering among the nations, for the sake of their repentance through the rod (Lev 27:32).

20.12.0.en: 40 For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord GOD, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things. 41 I will accept you with your sweet savour, when I bring you out from the people, and gather you out of the countries wherein ye have been scattered; and I will be sanctified in you before the heathen. 42 And ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall bring you into the land of Israel, into the country for the which I lifted up mine hand to give it to your fathers. 43 And there shall ye remember your ways, and all your doings, wherein ye have been defiled; and ye shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for all your evils that ye have committed. 44 And ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I have wrought with you for my name's sake, not according to your wicked ways, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord GOD."

20.13.0.en: After presenting a picture of Israel's turning aside to idolatry, as an ancient, violent and destructive turning aside in its results, and in spite of the dark and evil past, in the same chapter He dawns upon them with a future full of hope, of their return from captivity and their reform, as a symbol of man's return from the captivity of sin and the reform of his corrupt nature. He brings us into "mine holy mountain," into His sanctuaries, the high mountain, that is, into the Church of Christ, where we worship God in Christ Jesus, so that God smells our offerings as a sweet savour [41] and accepts us. It is a salvation not by our own merits but through free grace, for He says: "not according to your wicked ways, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord GOD" [44].

20.14.0.en: 45 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 46 "Son of man, set thy face toward the south, and drop thy word toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the south field; 47 And say to the forest of the south, Hear the word of the LORD; Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every green tree in thee, and every dry tree: the flaming flame shall not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north shall be burned therein. 48 And all flesh shall see that I the LORD have kindled it: it shall not be quenched." 49 "Then said I, Ah Lord GOD! they say of me, Doth he not speak parables?"

20.14.1.en: Although He dawned upon them with hope of their return and reform, He affirms the necessity of discipline first by the fiery destroying sword of Nebuchadnezzar. He begins with a supernatural fire in the southern region, the fire of bitter discipline, until it burns all the thorns of sin.

20.14.2.en: He begins with the south (Teman), the southern desert, as a sign of the discipline of the southern kingdom (Judah and Jerusalem).

20.15.0.en: The prophet turned his face toward the south [46-47], that is, toward the land of Israel, to see as from afar the forests of Lebanon... proclaiming: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every green tree in thee, and every dry tree: the flaming flame shall not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north shall be burned therein" [47]. Thus God pours out the fire of His judgment on them that all may realize His holiness and His justice.

20.16.0.en: The prophet ends the chapter by saying: "Ah Lord GOD! they say of me, Doth he not speak parables?" [49]. This is the state of the soul that is slack in its search for its Savior, for it finds His speech obscure parables. As St. Ambrose says in his comment on the words of the Song: ["By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not" (Song 3:1). (She seeks Him by night because He speaks in parables, for He made darkness His dwelling, and "night unto night sheweth knowledge" (Ps 19:3)... but she does not find Him in this way...].

20.16.1.en: Take my rebellion away from me!

20.16.2.en: * You are all love, my God, but I am a rebellious man!

20.16.3.en: Who can save me from my ungrateful nature but You, O my Savior?!

20.16.4.en: * The elders asked You in the land of captivity, and You did not answer them, because You want their repentance and their returning to You.

20.16.5.en: I see in the speech of Your prophet with them my own ungrateful nature!

20.16.6.en: In Egypt they rebelled against You; they came out with a mighty hand and a high arm, but they carried the worship of the Egyptians in their hearts!

20.16.7.en: In the wilderness You were wonderful in Your care for them, but they did not cease to murmur.

20.16.8.en: In the Promised Land You were a fortress for them, but they disobeyed Your commandments and took part in the worship of idols!

20.16.9.en: You disciplined them by captivity... and there, instead of repentance, they were filled with abominations!

20.16.10.en: What, then, will You do with them?!

20.16.11.en: * Circumstances did not create murmuring, but I, by the corruption of my heart, make an excuse of every circumstance to declare my rebellion!

20.16.12.en: Save me, O Lord, from my continual ingratitude!

20.16.13.en: Establish me in You, that I may bear partnership in the divine nature.

20.16.14.en: By partaking of Your Body and Blood, which are given for me, I bear the nature of self-giving love!
